articles.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Sheets. Is Microsoft's Stock in Trouble?
articles.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Sheets, a new productivity tool that could compete with Microsoft Excel. However, the article argues Microsoft's stock is not in trouble due to its strong enterprise customer base, trust, and integrated Office suite. Microsoft 365 has over 450 million paid commercial seats, and businesses are unlikely to switch despite alternatives like Google Sheets.

articles.title: Here's How the S&P 500 Has Moved the Day After Each of Nvidia's Last 12 Reports
articles.summary: Analysis of the S&P 500's performance on the day after Nvidia's last 12 earnings reports shows the index rose 7 times and fell 5 times, with an average move of nearly zero (0.02%). While these days saw slightly larger swings than typical (0.76% vs 0.65% average), the data shows no predictable pattern for future market movements following Nvidia reports. Nearly all of the S&P 500's 67% gain since November 2023 came on non-report days.

articles.title: Why Does Palantir Stock Keep Going Down?
articles.summary: Palantir stock dropped 3.7% despite an analyst upgrade to a $248 price target, citing 92% revenue growth. The decline appears driven by broader AI sector panic following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, rather than company-specific issues. The author notes Palantir's fundamentals remain intact, though the stock trades at a premium valuation of 99x free cash flow.

articles.title: ServiceNow vs. Palantir Technologies: Comparing Steady Sales Scale Against Rapid Revenue Acceleration
articles.summary: Palantir Technologies is experiencing rapid revenue acceleration, growing Q3 2026 sales 96% year-over-year to $2.3 billion, driven by its commercial AI platform (AIP) which surpassed government revenue for the first time. ServiceNow maintains steady growth at 20.5% year-over-year in Q3 with $4.1 billion in revenue, but faces margin pressure as costs rise. Palantir's net income surged 49% while ServiceNow's declined year-over-year, explaining the significant valuation difference between the two companies.

articles.title: Infoblox Launches Australia Realm on AWS, Giving Regulated Organizations a Local Option for DDI Management and Preemptive Security
articles.summary: Infoblox announced the launch of its Australia realm, a new instance of the Infoblox Platform hosted on AWS in the Sydney region. This deployment provides Australian government agencies and enterprises with local data residency options for DNS, DHCP, and IP address management (DDI), along with threat defense capabilities, addressing regulatory requirements and the need for preemptive security in an era of AI-driven attacks.

articles.title: McDonald's Is Underperforming the S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100. Could January Mark a Turning Point?
articles.summary: McDonald's stock has surged 20% in the past month after falling 10% year-to-date, driven by investor optimism around a new value-oriented menu launching nationally in early 2027. The company is testing mix-and-match and fixed-price bundles at nearly 6,000 restaurants to address its loss of value proposition to lower- and middle-income customers. With strong Q3 results and Dividend King status, the stock could see further gains if the turnaround plan succeeds.

articles.title: Berkshire Hathaway's Railroad Earned 19% More Last Quarter. Its Insurance Underwriting Earned 43% Less.
articles.summary: Berkshire Hathaway's Q3 2026 earnings showed mixed results: insurance underwriting fell 43% while railroad freight operations (BNSF) rose 19.3%. The article highlights how Berkshire's diversified portfolio across multiple quality businesses allows it to weather underperformance in any single segment, demonstrating the strength of its multi-sector investment strategy under new CEO Greg Abel.

articles.title: 2 Stocks With Dividend Yields of 4% or More to Buy in November
articles.summary: The article recommends Pfizer and PepsiCo as overlooked dividend stocks offering yields above 4% in a market focused on AI and growth. Pfizer is diversifying into oncology with strong acquisition-driven growth, while PepsiCo is recovering from weight-loss drug concerns through international expansion and pricing power. Both stocks offer durability and reliable dividend income for long-term investors.

articles.title: Home Depot Accelerates Express Delivery: Can It Fuel Growth?
articles.summary: Home Depot has rolled out nationwide express delivery offering eligible products within three hours, with most deliveries completed in under an hour. Digital platform sales grew 11% in Q2'26, marking five consecutive quarters of double-digit growth. Competitors Lowe's and Floor & Décor are also enhancing delivery capabilities. However, housing affordability pressures and weak remodeling demand pose growth risks.

articles.title: Can ExxonMobil's Longtail Project Unlock Guyana's Growth Potential?
articles.summary: ExxonMobil approved its eighth Stabroek block project, Longtail, expected to begin operations in 2030 with capacity to process 1.2 Bscf of natural gas daily and produce up to 250,000 barrels of condensate. The project strengthens XOM's long-term production growth in Guyana. Meanwhile, Chevron is expanding Tengiz processing capacity by 20% and benefiting from Eastern Mediterranean projects, while TotalEnergies approved new offshore developments in Cyprus, Nigeria, and Azerbaijan to support 3%+ annual upstream production growth through 2030.

articles.title: Allegiant Travel Extends Bank of America Credit Card Partnership
articles.summary: Allegiant Travel Company (ALGT) has extended its decade-long co-branded credit card partnership with Bank of America. The Allways Rewards Visa card, which has won USA TODAY's Best Airline Credit Card award for eight consecutive years, is a key component of Allegiant's loyalty and ancillary revenue strategy. ALGT shares have gained 29.2% month-to-date, significantly outperforming the airline industry's 7.3% growth.

articles.title: AstraZeneca Secures US, EU Nod for New Myasthenia Gravis Drug Klygefa
articles.summary: AstraZeneca received FDA and EU regulatory approvals for Klygefa (gefurulimab), a complement C5 inhibitor for treating adults with AChR-positive generalized myasthenia gravis. The once-weekly, self-administered subcutaneous therapy showed significant improvements in daily activities versus placebo in Phase III trials. While the convenient dosing offers differentiation from AstraZeneca's existing IV therapies (Soliris and Ultomiris), Klygefa faces cannibalization risks and competition from other complement C5 inhibitors and alternative mechanism drugs.

articles.title: Can MCD Protect Margins Amid Mid-Single-Digit Food Inflation in 2027?
articles.summary: McDonald's expects mid-single-digit food and paper inflation in 2027 and plans to protect margins through selective pricing, value bundles, and operating efficiencies. Entry-level bundles covering over 40% of U.S. locations will launch nationally in early 2027, with existing Extra Value Meals showing 7% unit sales growth. Competitors like Starbucks and Dutch Bros are also managing cost pressures through margin initiatives and pricing strategies.

articles.title: PepsiCo Stock Drops 2.4% in 6 Months: Is More Downside Ahead?
articles.summary: PepsiCo (PEP) has underperformed its industry peers over the past six months, declining 2.4% as the company faces weak North American beverage volumes, rising input costs, and margin pressures. The company lowered its 2026 earnings guidance to 2.5-3.5% core EPS growth from the previous 5-7%, citing weaker margins and unfavorable business mix. While PEP trades at a discount valuation of 16.89X forward P/E, analysts remain concerned about its subdued growth outlook and profitability challenges.

articles.title: Target's AI Commerce Partnerships Open New Customer Opportunities
articles.summary: Target is partnering with OpenAI, Google Gemini, and other AI platforms to tap into the growing agentic commerce ecosystem. The retailer's AI-driven digital traffic grew 3.5 times faster than the industry in Q2 2026, though converting visits to purchases remains a challenge. Target's digital comparable sales increased 8.7% year-over-year, supported by improved inventory and customer experience initiatives.

articles.title: PRGS or MSFT: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
articles.summary: A comparison of Progress Software (PRGS) and Microsoft (MSFT) in the Computer-Software sector reveals that PRGS presents a better value opportunity. PRGS holds a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy) with a Value grade of A, featuring a forward P/E of 7.09 and P/B ratio of 3.38. MSFT has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a Value grade of C, showing a forward P/E of 26.31 and P/B ratio of 8.27. Value investors are likely to favor PRGS based on these metrics.

articles.title: Can Dollar General Reach Its Long-Term 6-7% Operating Margin Goal?
articles.summary: Dollar General reported Q2 operating profit growth of 29.2% with operating margin expanding to 6.8%, moving closer to its 6-7% long-term target. The company expects shrink and damages reductions to drive 50 basis points of incremental gross margin growth in FY26. DG shares outperformed the industry with an 11.7% gain over three months, and the stock trades at an attractive valuation with a forward P/E of 16.14 compared to the industry average of 30.18.

articles.title: Costco Hits 52-Week High on Strong Sales and Special Dividend
articles.summary: Costco reached a 52-week high of $1,109.50 with shares up 28.3% year-to-date, driven by strong October sales growth of 12.6% and digital sales surge of 22.5%. The company announced a $30 special dividend and $4B buyback program. However, its forward P/E ratio of 47.75 significantly exceeds the industry average of 30.19, suggesting much of the optimism may already be priced in and limiting near-term upside potential.

articles.title: Anti-Obesity Drugs Market Companies Analysis 2027: Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk Lead as Pfizer, Roche and Amgen Invest Billions to Challenge Them in a Market Headed for USD 64.96 Billion by 2035
articles.summary: The global anti-obesity drugs market is valued at USD 8.96 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 64.96 billion by 2035 at a 24.71% CAGR. Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk dominate with strong Q3 2026 results, while Pfizer, Roche, and Amgen are investing billions to compete. Key trends include oral GLP-1 formulations, higher efficacy rates (>20% weight loss), and significant manufacturing capacity investments.

articles.title: CAT's Sales Volumes Rise Across Segments: Can Growth Continue?
articles.summary: Caterpillar (CAT) reported $7.64 billion in revenue gains from higher sales volumes during the first nine months of 2026, with Construction Industries contributing $4.1 billion and Power & Energy adding $2.5 billion. The company maintains mid-to-high-teens revenue growth expectations for the full year, supported by infrastructure spending, data center investments, and mining demand. CAT shares have outperformed the industry with 8.7% gains over the past year.

articles.title: J&J Stock Rallies More Than 10% in a Month: Time to Buy, Sell or Hold?
articles.summary: Johnson & Johnson's stock has rallied over 10% in a month, driven by better-than-expected Q3 2026 earnings and raised full-year guidance. The Innovative Medicine segment shows strong growth with new drug launches offsetting Stelara's patent expiration, but MedTech weakness, generic competition, and ongoing talc litigation remain concerns. Analysts recommend holding the stock for long-term investors despite near-term headwinds.

articles.title: Petrobras Stock After Q3 Earnings - Buy, Sell or Hold for Now?
articles.summary: Petrobras (PBR) reported Q3 revenues up 40.4% year-over-year with shareholder profit rising 28.4% and free cash flow climbing 33.2%. The company raised its annual production outlook to 3.3-3.4 MMBOE/d and cash-flow forecast to $45-$50 billion. However, profits declined sequentially from Q2, and rising capital spending poses risks. With 2026 EPS projected to surge 76.8% and PBR trading at a lower forward P/E than peers, analysts rate it a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), though state control and oil price volatility remain concerns.

articles.title: If a Stock Market Crash Is Coming in 2027, Warren Buffett’s Advice Makes My Next Move Clear
articles.summary: With market volatility returning and concerns about a potential 2027 stock market crash, the article advises investors to follow Warren Buffett's strategy: don't try to predict crashes, invest in quality businesses with strong fundamentals, and maintain a disciplined approach of regular contributions over time rather than attempting market timing.

articles.title: IBM vs. Jabil: Which Stock is Better Positioned for AI Growth Now?
articles.summary: Jabil appears better positioned than IBM for AI growth, with stronger projected growth rates (24.1% sales, 34.5% EPS vs IBM's 4.4% and 7.2%), better valuation metrics, and superior price performance. While IBM benefits from hybrid cloud and AI solutions, it faces intense competition from AWS and Azure plus threats from AI tools like Claude Code. Jabil gains from AI data center infrastructure demand with strong operational execution, though it faces competitive pressures and geopolitical headwinds.

articles.title: Bank of America Moves to Settle Fake-Accounts Lawsuit: What's Next?
articles.summary: Bank of America has reached a settlement in principle in a class-action lawsuit over unauthorized customer accounts opened by employees to meet sales targets. The settlement, pending court approval by January 11, 2027, could reduce legal costs and reputational risks, though the financial impact remains uncertain. BAC's shares have underperformed the industry in the past six months, and earnings estimates have been revised lower.

articles.title: Should iShares Core High Dividend ETF (HDV) Be on Your Investing Radar?
articles.summary: iShares Core High Dividend ETF (HDV) is a passively managed large-cap value ETF with $16.58 billion in assets and a low 0.08% expense ratio. The fund has delivered strong 2026 performance (+30.29% YTD) with a 3.09% dividend yield, though it carries a Zacks ETF Rank of 3 (Hold). Competitors like SCHD and VTV offer lower expense ratios and larger asset bases.

articles.title: Is Trending Stock Caterpillar Inc. (CAT) a Buy Now?
articles.summary: Caterpillar (CAT) has underperformed the broader market, declining 17.9% over the past month compared to the S&P 500's 3.1% decline. Despite strong earnings growth expectations (+43.4% for current fiscal year) and consistent beats on earnings and revenue estimates, the stock received a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating due to recent downward revisions in consensus estimates. The company is valued at par with peers and is expected to perform in line with the broader market in the near term.

articles.title: Implied Volatility Surging for Home Depot Stock Options
articles.summary: The Home Depot (HD) is drawing attention from options traders due to high implied volatility on December 2026 $175 calls, suggesting expectations of significant price movement. However, the company holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with mixed analyst sentiment—two analysts raised earnings estimates while three lowered them over the past 60 days, keeping consensus estimates relatively flat.

articles.title: JPMorgan vs. Truist: Which Bank Stock Has More Upside in 2027?
articles.summary: JPMorgan and Truist are pursuing distinct strategies heading into 2027. JPM targets $107B in NII with 3.7% projected earnings growth, while TFC focuses on efficiency and profitability with 4.8% projected earnings growth. JPM trades at a premium valuation (3.24X tangible book) reflecting its diversified business, while TFC's lower valuation (1.87X) offers potential upside if its restructuring initiatives succeed. Both stocks carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating.

articles.title: Not SpaceX. Not Blue Origin. The Space Stock That Just Raised Its Launch Price to $70 Million -- and Still Sold Out.
articles.summary: Rocket Lab raised its Neutron rocket's base launch price to $70 million from $55 million and still booked a record quarter with eight missions totaling over $515 million in contracts, all before the rocket's first flight. The company achieved record Q3 revenue of $267.8 million (up 73%) and a backlog of $3.57 billion (up 52%), demonstrating strong pricing power and customer demand despite Neutron's delayed debut to 2027.

articles.title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Visa, ExxonMobil Holdings and Pfizer
articles.summary: Zacks analysts reviewed three major stocks on November 16, 2026. Visa benefits from strong brand and digital transaction growth but faces profitability pressures from rising expenses. ExxonMobil gains from low-cost production and expansion opportunities but remains exposed to commodity volatility. Pfizer struggles with patent expirations and subdued near-term growth, though pipeline investments in oncology and obesity offer longer-term potential.

articles.title: Should You Buy Nvidia Stock Now That Jensen Huang Has Resigned? Here’s What I’m Doing.
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following news of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, causing the stock to fall 30% from its all-time high. However, the article argues Nvidia's core business remains strong with 70% projected revenue growth in 2027 and AI hyperscaler spending expected to reach $1.3 trillion. Trading at just 10.6x forward earnings, the author views Nvidia as a strong buy despite leadership uncertainty, though warns that hiring a finance-background CEO could be problematic.

articles.title: Home Sales Just Sank to a 16-Year Low. Here’s What This Means for Home Depot and Lowe’s Investors.
articles.summary: U.S. existing-home sales hit a 16-year low in October at 3.75 million units, driven by a 7.11% mortgage rate that discourages home purchases. This housing market weakness directly impacts Home Depot and Lowe's, which saw muted same-store sales growth of 1.7% and 0.2% respectively in Q2. Both stocks trade 20% below their peaks, and investors must wait longer for fundamental improvements as inflation and higher interest rates continue to pressure demand for home improvement projects.

articles.title: Why Investors Should Own Businesses That Can Win Under Any Administration
articles.summary: The article argues that long-term investors should focus on businesses resilient to political cycles rather than trying to time investments around elections. With U.S. elections every two years, political winds shift rapidly. The author recommends three stocks representing different sectors: Procter & Gamble (consumer staples), Federal Realty (REITs), and NextEra Energy (utilities)—all businesses whose demand remains stable regardless of which political party is in power.

articles.title: This 27-Year-Old Warning From Warren Buffett Is More Important Than Ever for Investors Today
articles.summary: Warren Buffett's 1999 warning about investing in transformative technologies remains relevant for AI investors today. While technologies like the internet, automobile, and aviation have dramatically impacted society, they haven't necessarily created profitable investments. Buffett's key lesson: success depends not on industry growth potential, but on identifying companies with durable competitive advantages (wide moats). The article examines how this applies to AI investments, highlighting Alphabet's strong moat versus commodity server providers and frontier AI labs facing intense competition.

articles.title: Rigetti Computing vs. SoundHound AI: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares two emerging technology stocks: Rigetti Computing, a quantum hardware developer, and SoundHound AI, a conversational AI platform provider. While Rigetti faces challenges with early-stage quantum technology and declining revenue ($7.1M, down 34.3%), SoundHound demonstrates stronger commercial traction with 99.4% revenue growth to $168.9M and a path to profitability by late 2027. The analyst recommends SoundHound as the better 2027 investment due to more consistent revenue scaling, superior valuation metrics (6.8x P/S vs 251.1x), and nearer-term profitability prospects.

articles.title: Investors: If a Market Correction Is Coming, This 1 Move Will Make or Break Your Portfolio
articles.summary: As the Nasdaq-100 enters correction territory down 11% from highs, the article emphasizes that diversification is the critical strategy to mitigate portfolio pain during market downturns. Investors should maintain 20-50 stocks across different sectors, asset classes, and geographies rather than concentrating bets in high-risk areas like AI infrastructure stocks.

articles.title: Why Fervo Energy Stock Surged This Week
articles.summary: Fervo Energy stock surged 29% this week following the announcement of a landmark 15-year power purchase agreement with Google to supply 396 megawatts of geothermal electricity. The deal expanded the company's contracted revenue backlog to $11.9 billion, while operational progress at its Utah Cape Station facility included the commercial operation of its first 33-megawatt GeoBlock. Despite the positive developments, the stock remains down 73% from its 52-week high, and investors should note the company is still pre-revenue with significant execution risks.

articles.title: Vanguard Economists Say: Inflation Might Be Better Than It Looks. Here's Why That's Good News for Stocks.
articles.summary: Vanguard economists forecast that core inflation could drop to 2.5% by April 2027 due to tariff roll-off effects, suggesting the Federal Reserve may not need to raise interest rates significantly higher. This optimistic outlook could be bullish for stocks, particularly tech and growth stocks, if inflation stabilizes and interest rates remain steady or decline in 2027.

articles.title: SHAREHOLDER ALERT: Bronstein Gewirtz & Grossman, LLC Announces Class Action Against Bank of America Corporation (NYSE: BAC) — Investors Who Suffered Losses Are Encouraged to Contact the Firm
articles.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Bank of America Corporation for alleged securities fraud. The complaint alleges that BAC made false and misleading statements regarding systemic weaknesses in its Bank Secrecy Act and Anti-Money Laundering compliance program, failure to properly monitor trillions in transactions, and inadequate remediation of compliance deficiencies. Investors who purchased BAC securities between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026 may be eligible to recover losses, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 15, 2026.

articles.title: Warren Buffett Remains Berkshire's Largest Individual Shareholder, With Forbes Pegging His Personal Fortune at About $149 Billion as of Mid-November. Here's Why Record Buybacks Are Quietly Growing His Stake Further.
articles.summary: Warren Buffett's net worth stands at $149 billion, representing nearly 12% of Berkshire Hathaway's $1.3 trillion market capitalization. CEO Greg Abel oversaw record $9.6 billion in share buybacks during Q3 2026, more than double Q2's total, which increases Buffett's ownership stake. However, Berkshire's massive $352 billion cash pile remains a drag on intrinsic value growth, as the company awaits high-return investment opportunities.

articles.title: U.S. Bancorp Pays Out 40% of Its Profit as Dividends. Here's How Much Room It Has to Raise Them.
articles.summary: U.S. Bancorp is highlighted as one of the best dividend stocks among banks, with a 3.54% yield, 16 consecutive years of dividend increases, and a sustainable 40% payout ratio. The stock has outperformed the S&P 500 with 17% year-to-date gains and 33% returns over the past year, indicating the high yield is supported by strong performance rather than a declining stock price.

articles.title: Which Bank ETF Is the Better Buy: State Street’s Regional Banking KRE or First Trust’s FTXO?
articles.summary: The article compares two banking ETFs: State Street's KRE (regional banking focus with 167 holdings) and First Trust's FTXO (mega-cap heavy with 50 holdings). KRE is recommended as the better choice for most long-term investors due to its lower 0.35% expense ratio, higher 2.2% dividend yield, broader diversification, and stronger 1-year performance of 22% versus FTXO's 16.6%. FTXO suits investors betting on mega-bank outperformance but carries concentration risk.

articles.title: Should You Invest Now or Wait Until 2027? Here's What a Century of History Says.
articles.summary: Despite recent market volatility and a 3-6% pullback from October highs, historical data spanning a century suggests investors should remain invested rather than wait for better timing. Studies show that consistent investing, even at market peaks, outperforms market timing strategies. The S&P 500 has averaged 10% annual returns including all recessions and bear markets, with the key being continuous market participation.

articles.title: 21 Financial Institutions Plan to Launch a New Dollar Stablecoin in 2027. Who Will Be the Biggest Winners and Losers?
articles.summary: Project Faro, backed by 21 financial institutions including Goldman Sachs and Citigroup, plans to launch a new dollar stablecoin in 2027 with $270 million in funding. This move, along with the Open USD consortium, intensifies competition in the $300 billion stablecoin market currently dominated by Tether and USDC. While payment processors like Mastercard and Visa stand to benefit, Circle Internet Group (USDC issuer) and PayPal face potential headwinds from these well-funded rivals.

articles.title: Microsoft Ignite Starts Nov. 17. Will Microsoft Update Its Paid Copilot Seat Count?
articles.summary: Microsoft is hosting its annual Ignite conference starting Nov. 17, where investors are watching for an update on paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seat counts. The company reported over 30 million paid seats in July but skipped this metric in its October earnings report, instead focusing on usage statistics like a 50% increase in daily users. Analysts are uncertain whether Copilot's revenue contribution justifies Microsoft's current valuation at 29x adjusted earnings.

articles.title: Is Credo Technology a Better AI Networking Buy Than Broadcom?
articles.summary: The article compares Broadcom and Credo Technology as AI networking investments. Broadcom, a $1.7T chip giant, offers stability with projected AI revenue reaching $230B by 2028 and pays a dividend. Credo Technology, a smaller $25B networking specialist, delivers triple-digit revenue growth and focuses on optical and copper connectivity for data centers. The choice depends on investor risk tolerance: Broadcom suits conservative investors seeking stability, while Credo appeals to growth-focused investors willing to accept volatility.

articles.title: Home Depot vs. Walmart: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares Home Depot and Walmart as investment options for 2027. Home Depot focuses on professional contractors and DIY customers with higher margins (8.4%) and a 2.7% dividend yield, while Walmart leverages its massive scale and grocery business with lower margins (3%) and 0.76% dividend yield. The author recommends Home Depot for 2027 based on its higher profitability, better dividend yield, and solid performance relative to the S&P 500, despite Walmart's stronger recent outperformance.

articles.title: Is Boeing an Undervalued Dividend Stock to Buy Right Now?
articles.summary: Boeing faces challenges in ramping up production amid regulatory pressure, raising questions about whether it represents an undervalued dividend investment opportunity at current levels.

articles.title: ROSEN, A RANKED AND LEADING LAW FIRM, Encourages Bank of America Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - BAC
articles.summary: Rosen Law Firm is soliciting Bank of America investors who purchased stock between August 1, 2025 and October 13, 2026 to join a securities class action lawsuit. The lawsuit alleges that Bank of America failed to disclose systemic weaknesses in its subsidiary's BSA/AML compliance program, resulting in improper monitoring of trillions in transactions and inaccurate suspicious activity reports. The firm claims defendants made materially false statements about compliance failures and expected costs, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 15, 2026.

articles.title: Kraft Heinz vs. PepsiCo: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: Kraft Heinz and PepsiCo are compared as investment options for 2027. Kraft Heinz faces challenges with declining revenue, a $3.5 billion net loss, and high customer concentration with Walmart. PepsiCo demonstrates stronger fundamentals with 6.4% revenue growth, $10.9 billion net income, and a more diversified portfolio. The analyst recommends PepsiCo as the better defensive dividend stock despite both companies underperforming the broader market.

articles.title: This Under-the-Radar Stock Is Behind Steak 'n Shake's MAHA-Driven Growth. Should You Buy?
articles.summary: Biglari, which owns Steak 'n Shake, has seen impressive same-store sales growth of 19.1% in Q3 2026 after adopting MAHA-aligned menu changes like beef tallow fries and grass-fed beef. However, the company remains a speculative investment as it continues closing underperforming locations, restaurant revenue growth lags overall revenue growth, and Biglari is a diversified conglomerate rather than a pure-play restaurant company.

articles.title: Nvidia's Ousted CEO Said a 1-Gigawatt Data Center Delay Costs $10 Billion a Quarter. Here's Why That Matters for Power Stocks.
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang highlighted that a three-month delay in constructing a 1-gigawatt data center costs $10 billion in lost revenue, underscoring energy as a critical bottleneck for AI growth. Multiple financial institutions warn that power availability is the binding constraint for AI expansion. The article recommends investing in power companies like Constellation Energy and Bloom Energy as lower-risk alternatives to AI stocks for gaining exposure to the AI economy.

articles.title: ASML vs. NVIDIA: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares ASML and NVIDIA as investment options for 2027. ASML, which holds a near-monopoly on advanced lithography equipment, generated $43.6B in revenue with strong growth and solid financial metrics. NVIDIA, a GPU leader for AI applications, posted $303B in revenue with 83.4% growth but faces regulatory risks and customer concentration concerns. The author recommends ASML for 2027 due to its defensible market position, while suggesting caution on NVIDIA given recent leadership changes and pending investigations.

articles.title: Forget SpaceX: This Potential Blockbuster IPO Has Attracted $26 Billion From AI Giants
articles.summary: Anthropic is set to go public with a $1.4 trillion valuation and has attracted $26 billion in commitments from major AI companies including Alphabet, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC. While the company shows strong revenue growth of 1,206% year-over-year, it remains unprofitable with significant losses. The investments signal confidence in Anthropic's potential, though valuation concerns and execution risks remain.

articles.title: American Express vs. S&P Global: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares American Express and S&P Global as investment options for 2027. American Express operates a closed-loop payment network with $72.2B in FY2025 revenue and 15% net margins, benefiting from premium consumer spending. S&P Global provides financial ratings and data with $15.3B in FY2025 revenue and superior 29.2% net margins, benefiting from passive investing growth. The author recommends American Express for its younger customer base and different growth driver, while S&P Global suits investors seeking exposure to passive investing trends.

articles.title: 5 Dividend Stocks to Buy and Hold Forever
articles.summary: The article recommends five dividend stocks suitable for long-term buy-and-hold investors: Johnson & Johnson, Medtronic, Procter & Gamble, Federal Realty Investment Trust, and Realty Income. All five companies have strong dividend track records with at least 32 years of consecutive annual increases, combined with well-run underlying businesses that generate reliable income streams.

articles.title: Is CoreWeave Stock a Buy After Its Latest Earnings?
articles.summary: CoreWeave delivered impressive Q3 earnings with 168% YoY revenue growth to $3.7B and a $132.5B customer backlog, but still reported a $709M net loss. While the company is executing well and raising guidance, it faces challenges converting growth into profits due to massive capital investments in infrastructure and high financing costs. The stock is viewed as a speculative opportunity after its recent sell-off, but remains risky for conservative investors until profitability improves.

articles.title: 5 Dividend Stocks With High Yields That Are Safer Than You Might Think
articles.summary: The article examines five high-yield dividend stocks that appear riskier than they actually are. Pfizer and Bristol Myers Squibb face normal pharmaceutical industry headwinds from patent expirations but maintain sustainable dividends through strong cash flows. REITs Realty Income and W.P. Carey are pressured by rising interest rates, but historical market adjustments should protect profitability. Hormel Foods, despite slow turnaround progress, has strong financials and backing from the Hormel Foundation, making its dividend safer than its yield suggests.

articles.title: Apple's Market Value Grew From $350 Billion to $4 Trillion During Tim Cook's 15 Years as CEO. Here's What That Growth Curve Means for Apple's Next Chapter Under John Ternus
articles.summary: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO after 15 years, during which the company's market value grew from $350 billion to $4.6 trillion. While new CEO John Ternus is unlikely to match Cook's exceptional returns, Apple remains well-positioned for growth through popular products like the iPhone 17 and new innovations like the iPhone Duo foldable smartphone, along with its strong services segment and shareholder capital returns.

articles.title: Novo Nordisk vs. Pfizer: Does a Weight Loss or Cancer Focused Pharma Stock Make a Better Buy for 2027?
articles.summary: The article compares Novo Nordisk and Pfizer as investment choices for 2027. Novo Nordisk dominates the high-growth obesity and diabetes treatment markets with blockbuster drugs like Wegovy and Ozempic, but faces pricing pressures and competition from rivals like Eli Lilly. Pfizer offers a diversified portfolio, stronger cash position ($14.3B vs $6.8B), and cheaper valuation, making it the better turnaround bet despite slower growth.
